_comentario: First Economics, Part 1 (autumn, days 1-65): the English text of each day of Aprendo economía -- the day's story ('historia', which the child reads; on Mondays it says the word of the week) and the text of its activity ('actividad', with its 'tipo'): the question, the cards, the sentences, the steps, the shop names, the lines of the money book, the 'prompt' and the 'checklist'. Everything else about the day (the picture, the activity, the things, the prices, the money, which box each card goes in, which sentence is true) is the one in content/q1.json, page by page: see cargar_traduccion in tools/gen_economia.py. And the words of the week ('semanas'), in English, for 'My economics dictionary'. British English, like First Words and First Numbers; the money is euros, written the English way: €5.

semanas.definicion: What something is worth to us: because it is useful, because it is beautiful, because there are few of them or because we love it.
Swapping one thing for another, without using money.
The coins and notes we use to buy and sell things.
When there is not enough of something for everyone who wants it.
The money we all pay together for the things we all share: pavements, parks, schools and hospitals.
Letting someone have something to use, so that they give it back afterwards.
Using something again, instead of throwing it away.
What we must have to live well: food, clothes, a home, going to the doctor. Something we would like to have, but do not need, is a want.
The money we keep today to use later on.
What someone gets for doing something good or useful.
What you have to pay for something.
A group of people who work together: each one does a part.
Something you give to someone without asking for anything in return.

dias.historia: One Saturday, Grandma Rosa gives Lucía a very old magnifying glass with a wooden handle. It belonged to her father, who mended clocks. In a shop it would not cost much, but to Lucía it has great value.

actividad.prompt: Draw something that has great value to you, even if it does not cost much money.

dias.historia: On Sunday, Lucía looks at a leaf from the garden through the magnifying glass, and finds its tiny paths. A magnifying glass is for seeing the smallest things. Something that is good for something is useful.

actividad.pregunta: Why does each thing have value?

dias.historia: Grandma says that her father's workshop was full of clocks of every kind. The oldest ones were worth a lot of money, because there were very few of them left. When there are only a few of something, they are worth more.

frases: An old thing is never worth anything.
Some things are worth a lot even if they cost little money.
When there are very few of something, they are worth more.
Everybody wants the same things.

dias.historia: Dani wants to swap his toy car for Lucía's magnifying glass. Lucía says no: to her, the magnifying glass is worth much more, because it belonged to Grandma's father.

actividad.pregunta: Why does each one have value?
pares: it is useful when it rains

dias.historia: At night, Lucía puts the magnifying glass in her treasure box. In it she keeps things that are not worth any money, but that she would not swap for anything: a shell, a stone and a photo of Toby.

checklist: I know what value means.
I know that some things have value because they are useful.
I know that some things have value because we love them.
actividad.prompt: Draw your treasure box, with the things you love most.

dias.historia: On Monday a new boy, Hugo, joins the class. He comes from a town by the sea. At break time, Hugo swaps a shell for two of Sofía's cards. Swapping one thing for another without money is called barter.
Sofía loves shells, and Hugo loves animal cards. That is why the swap is good for both of them: each one gives what they have spare and keeps what they want most.
Lucía wants Hugo's blue pencil, but Hugo does not like anything Lucía has. If neither of them wants what the other one has, there can be no swap.

actividad.pregunta: Is it a swap?
cosas: I'll swap my sandwich for your apple.
Mum pays for the bread with a coin.
I give you a card, and you give me a marble.
I swap my pencil for your rubber.

dias.historia: Hugo says that, many years ago, the fishermen in his town used to swap fish for bread. Today they sell their fish at the market, and with the money they buy the bread they want.
On Friday, Sofía shows Hugo the park in the neighbourhood, and Hugo gives her another shell. This time he does not want anything back: it is a gift, not a swap.

checklist: I know what barter is.
I know that when we barter, each one has to want what the other one has.
I can swap things without money.
actividad.prompt: Draw a swap: you, a friend, and the two things you swap.

dias.historia: Lucía, Sofía and Hugo start the Magnifying Glass Club. To buy a detective notebook, each of them puts some money in a box: Lucía €2, Sofía €2 and Hugo €1.

actividad.pregunta: How much money is there in the club's box?

dias.historia: Money is easier than swapping. The man at the stationery shop does not want Hugo's shells, but he does want coins: with them, he can buy what he wants too.

frases: You can buy things with money.
Money grows on trees.
A €2 coin is worth more than a €1 coin.
A €5 note is worth less than a €2 coin.

dias.historia: The detective notebook costs €5, the same as the coins in the box. Hugo explains that five €1 coins are worth the same as a €5 note.

actividad.pregunta: What is worth the same?

dias.historia: Grandma Rosa gives the club a €10 note and two €2 coins. Sofía keeps it all in her piggy bank, because she is the club's treasurer.

actividad.pregunta: How much money does Grandma give the club?

dias.historia: With its first money, the club buys the notebook. On the first page, Lucía writes: “Magnifying Glass Club. Members: Lucía, Sofía and Hugo”.

checklist: I know what money is for.
I know how much each coin and each note is worth.
I can count money up to €20.
actividad.prompt: Draw the Magnifying Glass Club's notebook, and the money it cost.

dias.historia: Mum buys a packet of twelve biscuits. There are five people at home, and they all want lots: when there is not enough for everyone, there is scarcity.
On Tuesday, the biscuit jar is empty, and there is a trail of crumbs all the way to the living room. Who has eaten them? Now there are none left for tea.

frases: If there are few biscuits and lots of children, there are not enough for everyone.
When something is scarce, it can be shared out.
Water never runs out, even if we waste it.
If someone takes more than their share, someone else goes without.

dias.historia: For tea, Dad brings some tangerines, and Lucía suggests sharing them out equally. That way nobody gets cross, and nobody goes without.
In the playground there are three swings and eight children who want a go. Marta suggests taking turns: that way, even though swings are scarce, everyone gets to swing for a while.

actividad.pregunta: Is there enough for everyone?

dias.historia: Mum buys another packet of biscuits and hides it on the highest shelf. This time, everyone will get their share.

checklist: I know what scarcity is.
I can share things out between several people.
I know that, when there is not enough for everyone, we can take turns.
actividad.prompt: Draw how you would share 6 biscuits between 3 friends.

dias.historia: Some workers are mending the pavement in Lucía's street. Dad explains that he does not pay for it on his own: all the neighbours pay for it together, with their taxes.

actividad.pregunta: Who does it belong to?

dias.historia: Taxes pay for lots of things: Lucía's school, the local library, the doctors at the hospital and the street lamps.

frases: We all pay for the state school together.
The street lamps belong to just one family.
Taxes pay for the things we all share.
In the park, anyone can break whatever they like.

dias.historia: Some small footprints appear in the wet cement. Hugo says they must tell the workers: if the pavement gets spoilt, we all have to pay for it again.

actividad.pregunta: What does each one do?

dias.historia: The workers smooth the cement again, and put up a fence so that nobody steps on it. Lucía thinks that they work for all the neighbours too.

actividad.prompt: Draw something in your neighbourhood that belongs to everyone, and someone using it.

dias.historia: On Saturday, the pavement is dry and smooth. Dani rides along it on his scooter, and says it is the nicest pavement in the neighbourhood.

checklist: I know what taxes are.
I know which things belong to everyone.
I know that we must look after what belongs to everyone.
actividad.prompt: Draw your favourite park, with the things we all pay for together.

dias.historia: The local library is small, but it has lots of books. Tomás, the librarian, lends them for free: you take them home, and then you bring them back. That is a loan.

frases: At the library, you buy the books.
A borrowed book has to be given back.
If you look after what you borrow, they will lend it to you again.
A loan is a gift.

dias.historia: Tomás shows them a book about trees that someone brings back every Tuesday with a leaf inside. If every neighbour bought that book, they would spend much more than by sharing it.

actividad.pregunta: Do we buy it or borrow it?
cosas: a friend's bike, for an afternoon

dias.historia: In class, Hugo lends Lucía his blue pencil. At the end of the day, Lucía gives it back and says thank you: that way, next time, Hugo will lend it to her again.

actividad.pregunta: Who lends each thing?

dias.historia: Tomás has bought twelve new books for the library, and he wants to share them out between three shelves, the same number on each.

actividad.pregunta: Share 12 books between 3 shelves. How many go on each one? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: On Friday, Lucía takes her book back on time, and Tomás lends her another one. The library is like a big bookcase that we all share.

checklist: I know what a loan is.
I know that what we borrow must be given back.
I can look after what I borrow.
actividad.prompt: Draw the local library, with Tomás and lots of books.

dias.historia: Mum goes up to the attic to sort out some old boxes, and finds Dani's cot and a small bike. “These are still useful,” she says. “We can reuse them, or give them to someone who needs them.”

actividad.pregunta: Can it be used again?

dias.historia: Lucía's little bike is too small for her now, but it is just right for Dani. That way they do not need to buy another one, and the family saves money.

frases: Something you no longer use can be useful to someone else.
Everything old must be thrown away.
Reusing things helps us save money.
Only one person can ever use a bike.

dias.historia: At night there is a noise in the attic: knock, knock, knock. Dani is scared, but Lucía tells him the club will investigate. Meanwhile, Mum uses the empty boxes to keep toys in.

actividad.pregunta: What can you make with each thing?

dias.historia: Grandma keeps the buttons from old clothes in a tin. When someone loses one, she already has another, without going to the shop.

actividad.pregunta: Grandma has 16 buttons for 3 shirts. How many does she sew on each one? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: On Saturday, the family takes the clothes that no longer fit them to the neighbourhood charity sale. Other children will wear them this winter.

checklist: I know what reuse means.
I can find a new use for things.
I know that reusing things helps us save.
actividad.prompt: Draw something new you would make with a shoebox.

dias.historia: On Saturday, Dad goes to the market with Lucía and Dani. On the list there is bread, milk and fruit: they are needs, things we must have. Dani wants to add sweets.

actividad.pregunta: Do I need it, or do I want it?

dias.historia: At the fruit stall, everything has its price written on a label. Dad buys a kilo of apples and a kilo of tangerines.

actividad.pregunta: Dad buys a kilo of apples and a kilo of tangerines. How much does he pay?

dias.historia: Dad explains to Dani that sweets are not a need, but a want: he likes them, but he does not need them. Today, the money is for what is on the list.

frases: Bread is a need.
We need sweets to live.
A coat in winter is a need.
Everything we want is a need.

dias.historia: While Dad buys the fish, Dani carries the bread bag and Lucía checks the list. With a list, you do not forget anything, and you do not spend too much.

actividad.texto: Dad buys bread for €2 and fish for €9. How much does he spend altogether?

dias.historia: Back at home, Lucía crosses off everything they have bought. But something is missing: the bread bag has been left at the market!

checklist: I know what a need is.
I know what a want is.
I can write a shopping list.
actividad.prompt: Write and draw your shopping list for the weekend.

dias.historia: Today Lucía is eight, and Grandma Rosa gives her an envelope with €10 in it. Lucía decides to split it between three jars: one for spending, one for her savings and one for sharing.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía has €10. She puts €5 in the save jar and €3 in the spend jar. How much does she put in the share jar?

dias.historia: In the afternoon, Dad gives Lucía her pocket money for the week: a €5 note and two €2 coins. Lucía counts it all before putting it away.

actividad.pregunta: How much money does Dad give Lucía?

dias.historia: Lucía wants a detective book that costs €16. She already has €8 in her piggy bank. If she saves €2 every week, when will she be able to buy it?
Dani wants to save too, but every time he has a coin, he buys himself a sweet. Lucía explains that saving means waiting a little to have something better.

frases: Saving means keeping money for later.
If you spend all your money, you are saving too.
Saving a little every week adds up to a lot.
A piggy bank helps you spend faster.

dias.historia: Before going to sleep, Lucía shakes her piggy bank and listens to the coins. It rattles more than yesterday, and in a few weeks it will rattle even more.

checklist: I know what saving is.
I can split my money between three jars.
I can work out how long it takes to save for something.
actividad.prompt: Draw your piggy bank, and what you would like to buy with your savings.

dias.historia: Pedro cannot find his cat, Luna. The club makes a poster for the lamp posts: “Missing: white cat. Whoever finds her will get a reward”.

actividad.prompt: Draw the club's poster to find Luna, with the reward.

dias.historia: Pedro offers a €5 reward to whoever finds Luna. Dani says he would look for her anyway, without a reward, because he loves Luna very much.

frases: A reward is what you get for doing something useful.
We only help other people if they pay us.
A reward can be money, a present or a “thank you”.
You have to give a reward back.

dias.historia: Lots of neighbours look for Luna around the neighbourhood. Some look for her because of the reward, and others, above all, because they want to help Pedro.

actividad.pregunta: What is the reward for each thing?

dias.historia: While they look for Luna, the club counts the money in its box: they want to buy her a new bell when she turns up.

actividad.pregunta: How much money does the club have in its box?

dias.historia: Pedro says that, when Luna turns up, he will give the reward to the club. Lucía already knows what they will do with it: buy food for the cats at the animal shelter.

checklist: I know what a reward is.
I know that sometimes we help without a reward.
I can count the money in a reward.
actividad.prompt: Draw what you would do with a €5 reward.

dias.historia: Lucía's class goes to the dinosaur museum. The price of a child's ticket is €3, and the price of an adult's is €6.

actividad.texto: Marta pays for her ticket, which costs €6, and for Lucía's, which costs €3. How much does Marta pay altogether?

dias.historia: In the museum shop there is a rubber dinosaur that costs €4. Lucía has €5 in her pocket, and she wonders: can I afford it?
Lucía pays for the dinosaur with a €5 note. The woman at the till gives her back a €1 coin: that is her change, what is left over from what she paid.
Hugo wants to buy a pencil and a rubber dinosaur. Before going to pay, he adds up the prices, to know how much money he needs.
On the bus home, Lucía looks at her rubber dinosaur through the magnifying glass. It cost €4, but to her it is worth much more: it reminds her of a wonderful day.

checklist: I know what a price is.
I know if I can afford something.
I can work out the change.
actividad.prompt: Draw the museum shop, with the prices of the things.

dias.historia: The class is getting a Christmas play ready. Marta shares out the work: some paint, some sew the costumes and some rehearse. That way they work as a team.

actividad.pregunta: In what order do they get the play ready?

dias.historia: In a team, each one does what they do best: Sofía paints the scenery, Hugo does the lights, Lucía sews the star and Paco builds the stage. If each of them did everything alone, it would take ages.

actividad.pregunta: What does each one do?

dias.historia: The costumes need lots of buttons. Four mums share out the work, and each one sews on the same number.

actividad.pregunta: There are 20 buttons and 4 mums sewing. How many does each one sew on? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: On Tuesday, the golden star is not on the stage any more. Without it there can be no show, so the whole team starts looking for it.

frases: In a team, everyone does exactly the same thing.
A team takes less time than one person alone.
If someone makes a mistake, the team can help.
Teamwork means everyone does whatever they like.

dias.historia: On Friday, the show is a great success, and they all come out to bow together. Marta says the applause is for the whole team.

checklist: I know what a team is.
I know that in a team each one does a part.
I can put the steps of a job in order.
actividad.prompt: Draw the Christmas play put on by Lucía's class.

dias.historia: All term, someone has been leaving Lucía notes and riddles signed “Reader X”. They do not ask for anything in return: they are real gifts.

actividad.pregunta: Is it a gift?
cosas: You buy a storybook in a shop.
You swap a card for a marble.
You pay for bread at the baker's.

dias.historia: For Christmas, Lucía wants to make the presents herself: a bookmark for Dad and a drawing for Grandma. She only needs to buy some card and a ribbon.

actividad.texto: The card costs €2 and the ribbon €1. How much does Lucía spend on the presents?

dias.historia: Dani has no money for presents, so he gives hugs and songs. Grandma says they are her favourite presents.

frases: A gift has to cost a lot of money.
A drawing you made yourself can be a great gift.
If you ask for something back, it is not a gift any more.
People only give presents on birthdays.

dias.historia: On Thursday, Grandma brings a bag of sweets for the whole family. Lucía suggests sharing them out equally.

actividad.pregunta: There are 13 sweets for Dad, Mum, Lucía and Dani. How many does each one get? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: On Friday, the club unmasks Reader X: it is Dad, who writes the notes, and Dani, who makes up the riddles. Lucía thanks them with a hug, which is a gift too.

checklist: I know what a gift is.
I know that a handmade gift is worth a lot too.
I can share things out equally.
actividad.prompt: Draw a gift you could make yourself, without spending any money.
